strands.Description: Mastery-based additive reasoning from early structures through efficient mental, written, decimal and multi-step calculation.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Combine, partition, augment and reduce quantities; connect stories, part-whole models and equations.
levels.KeyRepresentations: equation, first-then-now, part-whole, story + choice
levels.ImplementationNotes: Preserve combining, partitioning, augmentation and reduction as distinct additive structures.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Use +0, -0, +1, -1, doubles/near doubles and commutativity; recognise efficient facts.
levels.KeyRepresentations: choice / statement, counters + equations, double frame, equation, paired equations, ten-frame
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.Skill: Fact families, inverse and missing numbers within 20
levels.DiagnosticIntent: Link addition/subtraction facts and solve equations with the unknown in different positions.
levels.KeyRepresentations: bar model, equation, fact family + choice, fact-family triangle, statement
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Make ten, partition the addend and connect ten frames, bead strings, number lines and equations.
levels.KeyRepresentations: choice + ten-frame, equation, number line, paired equations, statement, statement / equation, ten-frame, ten-frame + equation
levels.ImplementationNotes: Represent 'make ten' explicitly; show the partition of the addend.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Subtract through ten / from ten using partitioning and visual representations.
levels.KeyRepresentations: choice + number line, choice + ten-frame, equation, number line, statement, statement / equation, ten-frame, ten-frame + equation
levels.ImplementationNotes: Represent subtraction through ten explicitly; ensure the whole subtrahend is removed.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Compare quantities and measures; find difference by matching/counting on, not only take-away.
levels.KeyRepresentations: bar model, comparison towers, equation / generalisation, number line, statement, story / choice
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use comparison bars/towers and number-line distance, not only take-away imagery.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Add/subtract a one-digit number to/from a two-digit number, including crossing a tens boundary.
levels.KeyRepresentations: Dienes + number line, choice / misconception, equation, paired equations
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Use related facts and place value to add/subtract tens, including crossing 100 where appropriate.
levels.KeyRepresentations: equation, paired equations, place-value chart + Dienes, sequence / statement
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Add three one-digit numbers; use associative/commutative structure and make-ten pairs.
levels.KeyRepresentations: choice + grouping, equation, paired equations, statement, statement / choice, ten-frame groups
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Partition and recombine tens/ones using Dienes, bar/part-whole models and equations.
levels.KeyRepresentations: Dienes, bar model, choice / statement, equation, part-whole, statement
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Bridge/exchange ten when ones total 10 or more; connect mental and written representations.
levels.KeyRepresentations: Dienes, choice / statement, column algorithm, equation, part-whole + equation, place-value chart
levels.ImplementationNotes: Show 10 ones regrouped as 1 ten.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Partition the subtrahend or subtract by place value when each column is sufficient.
levels.KeyRepresentations: Dienes, choice / statement, equation, number line, part-whole
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Subtract across a ten using partitioning, counting on or exchange; compare efficient strategies.
levels.KeyRepresentations: Dienes, choice / statement, column algorithm, equation, number line, place-value chart
levels.ImplementationNotes: Show 1 ten exchanged for 10 ones; allow count-on where the difference is small.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Use complements, make-100 and related facts across the hundreds boundary.
levels.KeyRepresentations: choice / statement, hundred frame / bar, number line + hundred square, paired equations
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Add/subtract 1s, 10s and 100s; partition, compensate and use known facts efficiently.
levels.KeyRepresentations: choice / statement, number line, place-value chart + number line
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Align place value; add with no exchange, one exchange and multiple exchanges; explain regrouping.
levels.KeyRepresentations: column algorithm, column algorithm + place-value counters, place-value chart, place-value counters, statement / choice
levels.ImplementationNotes: Align digits by place value and make regrouping visible.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Align place value; exchange tens/hundreds, including exchange through zero; connect to partitioning.
levels.KeyRepresentations: column algorithm, column algorithm + place-value counters, number line + column comparison, place-value counters, statement, statement / choice
levels.ImplementationNotes: Support exchange through zero accurately.

levels.Skill: Written addition and subtraction with larger whole numbers
levels.DiagnosticIntent: Extend formal methods to four or more digits with accurate alignment and multiple exchanges.
levels.KeyRepresentations: column algorithm, equation, place-value chart + column, statement / choice
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.Skill: Efficient mental strategies with larger numbers
levels.DiagnosticIntent: Use compensation, adjustment, complements and place-value structure instead of defaulting to a written method.
levels.KeyRepresentations: bar / number line, number line / equation, paired equations, statement, strategy cards
levels.ImplementationNotes: Focus on efficient method choice, not just accuracy.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Estimate using rounding, check with inverse, detect unreasonable answers and identify calculation errors.
levels.KeyRepresentations: estimate comparison, fact family / equation, rounding + equation, worked example / statement
levels.ImplementationNotes: Use CPA/variation and preserve the equality structure shown in the bank.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Add/subtract tenths and hundredths, including money, with place-value alignment and complements.
levels.KeyRepresentations: decimal equation, money / bar model, money / coins, place-value chart + decimal counters, statement / decimal number line
levels.ImplementationNotes: Align decimal place values and decimal points.

levels.DiagnosticIntent: Interpret one- and multi-step additive problems; choose operations and efficient methods and solve missing-value problems.
levels.KeyRepresentations: bar model + context, bar model / flow diagram, equation / bar model, structure / strategy cards, worked problem / statement
levels.ImplementationNotes: Represent mathematical relationships; do not cue operations from keywords alone.

representation_guidance: Render equal-sized objects in labelled groups; for subtraction visibly remove/cross out only the specified amount.
Do not rely on colour alone; use group labels/patterns.
Use a fixed 2×5 frame. For bridging, show the first amount, the part that completes 10, then the remainder.
Use filled/empty shape differences plus labels.
Random dot arrangements when the purpose is ten structure.
Shows addition/subtraction as relationships between whole and parts
Whole and parts must remain visually linked. Allow the unknown in any node.
Label nodes; do not use colour alone.
Always putting the unknown in the same position.
Distinguishes change over time from static part–whole
Use three panels/arrows: starting amount, change, resulting amount.
Add text labels First / Then / Now.
Makes difference a comparison/distance rather than only take-away
Align bars/towers to the same baseline and visually show the unmatched section.
Exposes additive distance, partitioned jumps and efficient strategy
Use proportional spacing. Mark key boundaries such as 10, 100 or 0. Show jumps only when pedagogically intended.
Include numeric labels and arrow direction.
Non-proportional intervals unless explicitly an empty number line.
Connects calculation to unitising and exchange
Use unit cubes, tens rods and hundreds flats consistently. Depict 10 ones ↔ 1 ten and 10 tens ↔ 1 hundred.
Showing an exchange without preserving total value.
Makes alignment and exchange by place explicit
Columns must be labelled. Decimal charts must clearly separate ones/tenths/hundredths.
Aligning digits by string length instead of place value.
Connects compact written method to place value and exchange
Right-align whole-number digits by place. For decimals align decimal points. Show carried/exchanged values in the correct place.
Use large readable digits and clear column headings in teaching/reasoning variants.
Treating the algorithm as a pattern of digits with no place-value meaning.
Represents known/unknown relationships and supports operation choice
Lengths should broadly represent the relationship; label whole/parts clearly. Support comparison and part-whole variants.
Text labels as well as geometry.
Using keywords to reveal the operation.
Diagnoses efficient selection rather than merely accuracy
Offer meaningful strategies: mental/place value, count on, compensation, column method. Only one should be clearly most efficient where a single answer is expected.
Use text + simple icon; keyboard selectable.
Marking a valid alternative method wrong when the prompt does not ask for efficiency.
Prevents whole-number misconceptions and exposes tenths/hundredths
Use place-value chart, decimal counters or 10×10 grid when appropriate. Align decimal points and preserve zero placeholders.
Label place values and decimal point explicitly.
Aligning final digits instead of decimal place values.
Preserve the exact unknown position: e.g. __ + 7 = 15, 15 = __ + 7, 15 - __ = 8.
Do not rewrite every prompt as 'calculation = answer'. The varied equals-sign position is intentional.
Accept harmless numeric formatting differences where mathematically equivalent (e.g. 1000 and 1,000; 4 and 4.0 when appropriate).
For method-choice questions, use the wording and Mastery Focus to decide whether multiple valid strategies should be accepted.
